title: UN hears warning of ‘colonisation by data’
excerpt: United Nations, September 26 (IANS): World leaders have warned that Artificial Intelligence (AI) and control over data could create a new form of global domination, leaving developing countries dependent on technologies and rules designed elsewhere.Speakers from Asia, Europe, the Caribbean and the Indian and Pacific oceans welcomed AI’s potential. But they demanded a voice in global regulation, fair access to technology and protection for national languages, cultures and data.Bahamas Prime Minister Philip Davis offered the sharpest description of the danger.“This is colonisation by data. It does not arrive with ships and flags,” Davis told the UN General Assembly (UNGA).He said data had become the newest raw material in the global economy. Digital platforms, he argued, could take information from developing societies and return versions of their identities shaped elsewhere.Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman said existing technological inequality must not be allowed to spread into the next generation of digital systems.“We do not want today's digital divide to become tomorrow's artificial intelligence divide,” Rahman said.Bangladesh called for technology transfer, skills development and affordable access to modern technologies. It also urged the United Nations to adopt an effective policy framework so countries could benefit from the rapid expansion of AI and social media.The Maldives made a similar appeal for inclusive rule-making.“Every country must have a voice in shaping the global rules for AI,” Vice-President Hussain Mohamed Latheef said.He said AI could help small states overcome distance and scale, and improve health care, education and public services. But the digital future, he added, should not create new forms of dependence.Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama focused on manipulation, accountability and the use of AI by hostile actors.“The greatest danger is that it will obey the wrong human beings perfectly,” Rama said.He said no machine held democratic legitimacy and no algorithm inherited constitutional responsibility. AI, he warned, could multiply a falsehood at enormous speed and bury the truth without formally censoring it.South Korean President Lee Jae Myung described the AI revolution as both an opportunity and a crisis. Without preparation, he said, it could deepen inequality rather than spread prosperity.Saint Lucia warned that digital technology could create a hierarchy in which a small number of corporations and powerful states controlled systems used by everyone else.“The digital future must not be owned by a few. It must be governed for the benefit of all,” Prime Minister Philip J. Pierre said.UN Secretary-General António Guterres said the source of global influence was changing.“Today, power increasingly comes from data, computing capacity and algorithms. This new power is highly concentrated,” he said.Guterres called for information-sharing on emerging safety risks, common safeguards and a multilateral AI risk-management framework backed by independent oversight. He said every country should have a role through the United Nations.Tonga said it did not have to lead every technological race, but would help shape the rules governing new systems. It called for control over national data and warned that Pacific data, biodiversity and traditional knowledge must not fuel technological advances while returning little value to island communities.Guyana framed the issue as a test of whether innovation would improve ordinary lives.“Technology must not become the privilege of the few; it must become the servant of all humanity,” President Irfaan Ali said.India has a large information-technology industry, a rapidly expanding digital economy and one of the world’s biggest populations of technology users. New Delhi has also promoted its digital public infrastructure model as a way to widen access to public services across the Global South.

excerpt: અંબાજી: ભાદરવી પૂનમના મહામેળાના અંતિમ દિવસે DyCM હર્ષ સંઘવી યાત્રાધામ અંબાજીની મુલાકાતે પહોંચ્યા હતા. જ્યાં તેઓએ અંબાજી મંદિરના શિખર પર ધજા ચડાવી માતાજીના આશીર્વાદ મેળવ્યા હતા. આ દરમિયાન તેમણે મેળામાં ફરજ બજાવનારા પોલીસ કર્મચારીઓ, વહીવટી તંત્ર અને સ્વચ્છતા દૂતોની કામગીરીને પણ બિરદાવી હતી. ‘તેરા તુજકો અર્પણ’ કાર્યક્રમ અંતર્ગત મળેલી વસ્તુઓ તેના મૂળ માલિકોને પરત સોંપવામાં આવી હતી. આ સાથે મેળા દરમિયાન પ્રશંસનીય કામગીરી કરનારા પોલીસ અધિકારીઓ અને કર્મચારીઓને સન્માનપત્રો પણ અર્પણ કરવામાં આવ્યા હતા.મેળાની સફળતા અને સુરક્ષા બદલ માતાજી પ્રત્યે કૃતજ્ઞતા વ્યક્ત કરવા માટે પોલીસ વિભાગ દ્વારા વિશેષ ધજાયાત્રાનું આયોજન કરવામાં આવ્યું હતું. વાજતે-ગાજતે ધજાને મંદિર સુધી લઈ જવાઈ હતી. આ દરમિયાન પોલીસ કર્મચારીઓ અને તેમના પરિવારજનોએ પણ માતાજીના જયઘોષ સાથે ગરબાની રમઝટ બોલાવી હતી. હર્ષ સંઘવીએ અંબાજી મંદિરના શિખર પર ધજા રોહણ કર્યું હતું. ‘જય અંબે’ના ગગનભેદી નાદ વચ્ચે સમગ્ર યાત્રાધામ ભક્તિમય બની ગયું હતું.આ પ્રસંગે હર્ષ સંઘવીએ નિવેદન આપ્યું કે ભાદરવી પૂનમના મેળામાં પોલીસ અને વહીવટી તંત્રે અધિકારી તરીકે નહીં પરંતુ માઈ ભક્તોના સેવક તરીકે કામ કર્યું છે. લાખો શ્રદ્ધાળુઓની સુરક્ષા અને સુવિધા માટે દિવસ-રાત મહેનત કરનાર તમામ કર્મચારીઓ અભિનંદનના હકદાર છે. તેમણે જણાવ્યું કે આ વર્ષે ભાદરવી પૂનમના મેળામાં દર વર્ષની સરખામણીએ રેકોર્ડબ્રેક સંખ્યામાં ભક્તો પધાર્યા હતા. સાથે જ મેળાની સ્વચ્છતા જાળવવા માટે કાર્યરત સ્વચ્છતા દૂતોની કામગીરીને પણ તેમણે બિરદાવી હતી.

title: India to build 1st port-based Rs 2,300 crore e-methanol plant at Kandla to supply green fuel to ships
excerpt: India is setting up a Rs 2,300-crore e-methanol plant at Kandla, Gujarat to supply low-carbon fuel. The project, developed by Deendayal Port Authority and Assam Petro-Chemicals Ltd, aims for production of 150 tonnes per day. The initial unit of 50 tonnes per day is expected to be completed by January 2027. Alongside, additional capacity will be added at a cost of Rs 1,100 crore.

title: વડોદરામાં ગણેશ વિસર્જનમાં ધિંગાણું! બે જૂથ વચ્ચે મારામારીનો વીડિયો વાયરલ
excerpt: વડોદરા: ગણપતિ બાપ્પાને વિદાય દરમિયાન મારામારીના દ્રશ્યો સામે આવતા ચકચાર મચી ગઈ છે. વડોદરા શહેરના ખંડેરાવ માર્કેટ વિસ્તારમાં મોડી રાત્રે બે જૂથ વચ્ચે ઉગ્ર બોલાચાલી બાદ મારામારી સર્જાઈ હતી. સામે આવેલા વીડિયોમાં કેટલાક લોકો એકબીજા સાથે ઝપાઝપી અને મારામારી કરતા નજરે પડી રહ્યા છે. વિસર્જન યાત્રાના ઉત્સાહ વચ્ચે અચાનક સર્જાયેલી આ ઘટનાથી વિસ્તારમાં થોડા સમય માટે અફરાતફરીનો માહોલ સર્જાયો હતો.ઘટનાના દ્રશ્યો ત્યાં હાજર લોકોએ પોતાના મોબાઈલમાં કેદ કર્યા હતા અને વીડિયો સોશિયલ મીડિયામાં વાયરલ થતાં સમગ્ર મામલો ચર્ચાનો વિષય બન્યો છે વીડિયો વાયરલ થતાં જ પોલીસ તંત્ર પણ હરકતમાં આવ્યું છે. સમગ્ર ઘટનાને લઈને પોલીસ દ્વારા તપાસ શરૂ કરવામાં આવી છે અને મારામારી પાછળનું કારણ તેમજ સંડોવાયેલા લોકોની ઓળખ મેળવવાના પ્રયાસો હાથ ધરાયા છે.

title: શામળાજીમાં ભક્તિનો મહાસાગર! ભાદરવી પૂર્ણિમાએ ભક્તોનું ઘોડાપૂર ઉમટ્યું
excerpt: અરવલ્લી: આસ્થા, શ્રદ્ધા અને ભક્તિનું પવિત્ર પર્વ સમા ભાદરવી પૂર્ણિમાના દિવસે યાત્રાધામ શામળાજીમાં ભક્તોનું અદભૂત ઘોડાપૂર જોવા મળ્યું હતું. મોડી રાતથી જ હજારો ભક્તો પગપાળા યાત્રા કરીને ભગવાન શામળિયાના દર્શન માટે પહોંચ્યા હતા. ધાર્મિક માન્યતા અનુસાર ભાદરવા સુદ પૂર્ણિમાથી શ્રાદ્ધ પક્ષનો પ્રારંભ થાય છે અને આ દિવસ પિતૃઓના મોક્ષ માટે વિશેષ મહત્વ ધરાવે છે. તેથી ભક્તોએ ભગવાન શામળિયાના દર્શન કરીને પોતાના પિતૃઓના કલ્યાણ અને મોક્ષ માટે પ્રાર્થનાઓ અર્પણ કરી હતી...વહેલી સવારથી જ મંદિર પરિસરમાં ભક્તોની લાંબી કતારો જોવા મળી હતી. ભક્તોના ભારે ધસારાને ધ્યાનમાં રાખીને મંદિર ટ્રસ્ટ દ્વારા મંદિર નિયત સમય કરતાં એક કલાક વહેલું ખોલવામાં આવ્યું હતું. જેથી ભક્તોને સરળતાથી દર્શનનો લાભ મળી શકે. પગપાળા આવતા યાત્રાળુઓ માટે રસ્તામાં વિવિધ સેવાકીય કેમ્પો અને વિસામાઓનું આયોજન પણ કરવામાં આવ્યું હતું. જ્યાં ભક્તોને પાણી, નાસ્તો અને અન્ય જરૂરી સુવિધાઓ પૂરી પાડવામાં આવી હતી. ભક્તિના આ મહાપર્વે શામળાજી ધામમાં દિવસભર હરિનામનો ગુંજારવ સંભળાતો રહ્યો હતો અને અંદાજે એક લાખથી વધુ ભક્તોએ ભગવાન શામળિયાના દર્શન કરીને ધન્યતા અનુભવી હતી.

title: Talent tracker: Leadership changes that made news this week
excerpt: New Delhi: The past week brought a number of leadership changes across the industry, with senior executives stepping into new roles, taking on broader responsibilities and moving to new organisations. The developments covered marketing, communications, strategy, product, sales, media and business functions. Sachin Sharma exits LinkedIn as Director, Marketing Solutions after over six years Sachin Sharma has left LinkedIn after six-and-a-half years as Director, Marketing Solutions. Announcing the move on LinkedIn, Sharma said he is taking a break and has not disclosed his next role. At LinkedIn, he managed relationships with enterprise advertisers in India. This was his second stint at the company, having rejoined in April 2020 after working in advertising sales and brand partnerships at ByteDance. Earlier, Sharma worked with Airbnb India on host acquisition and supply partnerships, and spent over five years at Google across online sales and channel partnerships. WPP starts CFO hunt; Joanne Wilson to serve 12-month notice WPP has begun searching for a new Chief Financial Officer after Joanne Wilson accepted the same role at Diageo. Wilson will remain WPP’s CFO and Executive Director during the search. She has a 12-month notice period, but WPP has not set a departure date. Diageo said Wilson will join its Board and Executive Committee in 2027, succeeding Nik Jhangiani as CFO. Jhangiani will remain in the post until the handover. Dentsu India names Santosh Mishra Managing Partner, Client Management Dentsu India has appointed Santosh Mishra as Managing Partner, Client Management. He will report to Ajay Gupte, Chief Operating Officer, South Asia. Mishra will oversee key client relationships and work with teams across media, creative, data and technology. He joins from Wavemaker, where he was Managing Partner, Digital. He previously spent nearly a decade at iProspect and held roles at Publicis and Reliance Money. India Today Group elevates Sakshi Kohli to CEO, Luxury and Lifestyle Business (L-R) Sakshi Kohli, Radhika Mehta and Kamalinee Chatterjee India Today Group has redesignated Sakshi Kohli as CEO of its Luxury and Lifestyle Business, adding India Today Spice to her remit. Kohli will continue to oversee Harper’s Bazaar India, Cosmopolitan India, Hello! India and Brides Today. With India Today Spice, the portfolio now comprises five brands. Ruchika Mehta, Editor of Hello! India and Brides Today, will also become Editor of India Today Spice. Kamalinee Chatterjee, Vice President, Sales, will take on sales responsibility for the title and lead sales across the five brands. Cilicant appoints Prabhsharan Kaur to lead marketing in India and global markets Cilicant has appointed Prabhsharan Kaur as Director, Marketing, India & Global Markets. She will oversee marketing and brand communications across the company’s domestic and international markets, including work related to its active packaging business. Kaur joins from SKF, where she handled corporate communications, brand and public relations across India and other markets. Before that, she spent more than eight years at Avery Dennison in marketing and communications roles covering South Asia and Sub-Saharan Africa. Shantanu Chauhan joins Angara as Vice President - Brand, Global Shantanu Chauhan Shantanu Chauhan has joined Angara Ecommerce as Vice President, Brand, Global. He will lead the company’s brand work across international markets and will be based in Jaipur, according to his LinkedIn announcement. Chauhan joins after more than 10 years at Noise. Most recently, he was Director, Marketing (Brand & Growth), with responsibilities spanning brand marketing, direct-to-consumer sales and e-commerce. Before Noise, he worked on alliances, social media and affiliate marketing at DailyObjects. Earlier in his career, he held a marketing role at Songdew Media. Ram Gopalakrishnan takes charge of Vadilal’s international business Ram Gopalakrishnan took over as CEO of Vadilal Industries USA in August 2026, leading the company’s international business. He announced the move on LinkedIn. Before joining Vadilal, Gopalakrishnan held digital commerce and growth roles at Ethos Pet Brands. He previously led direct-to-consumer and omnichannel health and nutrition brands at Nestlé Health Science. His earlier experience includes brand and e-commerce roles at Clorox and Procter & Gamble, as well as a stint at Unilever. He began his career in engineering at Micron Technology and Intel. Monks names Nirvik Singh CEO of EMEA Marketing Services Monks has appointed Nirvik Singh as CEO of EMEA Marketing Services, effective October 1, 2026. He will oversee operations across Europe, the Middle East and Africa and join the company’s international executive leadership team. Singh will work with EMEA Chief Revenue Officer Alex Oberberg and regional managing directors across the company’s brand strategy, creative, content, media and technology services. He joined the board of Monks’ parent company, S4Capital, as an independent non-executive director in May 2025 and will leave the board when he takes up the executive role. Singh previously served as Global Chief Operating Officer and President, International, at Grey Group. Volvo Cars appoints Škoda chief Klaus Zellmer as President and CEO Volvo Cars has appointed Škoda Auto chief Klaus Zellmer as its next President and Chief Executive Officer. He will take over no later than October 1, 2027. Current CEO Håkan Samuelsson will work with the board on the transition. Zellmer has more than 30 years of automotive experience. Before joining Škoda, he oversaw marketing, sales and after-sales at Volkswagen Passenger Cars. He also spent more than two decades at Porsche, including as CEO of its German and North American businesses. Former Renault India communications head Nabeel A Khan joins MarkNext Group as CEO MarkNext Group has appointed Nabeel A Khan as Group Chief Executive Officer and Editor-in-Chief. He will oversee its communications advisory businesses and lead the launch and editorial strategy of a new media venture covering India, the Middle East and Africa. Khan joins after serving as Deputy Vice-President and Head of Public Affairs, PR and Communications at Renault India. He previously worked with Motherson Group in the Middle East. Before moving into corporate communications, Khan spent more than a decade in journalism. He was the founding editor of ETAuto at The Economic Times and earlier held editorial roles at Network18 and IANS. Ankit Dhameja moves to WPP Media as SVP Strategy, takes Google India mandate WPP Media has appointed Ankit Dhameja as Senior Vice President, Strategy, with responsibility for leading strategy for Google India. He announced the move on LinkedIn. Dhameja joins after more than six years at Deloitte, where he worked on strategy and research across technology and media. Before that, he spent five years at BBC News as Senior Manager, Data and Insights, covering audience, advertising impact and market research for Asia-Pacific and global teams. Earlier in his career, Dhameja was Manager, Research and Marketing, for CNN IBN and IBN7 at Network18. He also worked as a senior media planner at Mindshare. Karan Yadav takes charge as Indian Super League’s CEO Karan Yadav has been appointed Chief Executive Officer of the Indian Super League (ISL), he announced on LinkedIn. He joins after serving as Chief Commercial Officer at JSW Sports from April 2023 to September 2026. Yadav previously handled sponsorships and activations at ACKO and held sports and content roles at Wavemaker and IOS Sports & Entertainment. At JSW Sports, his work included the Neeraj Chopra Classic and partnerships across several sports leagues. The appointment comes as the ISL shifts to a club-led commercial structure. Under an arrangement announced in July, clubs will hold the league’s commercial rights, while the All India Football Federation will retain administrative control and oversight of key operations. The 2026-27 season is set to return to a home-and-away format. Kanika Juneja steps down as Maggi Noodles' category marketing head at Nestlé Kanika Juneja has stepped down as Category Marketing Head for Maggi Noodles at Nestlé after six years with the company. She announced her departure on LinkedIn and has not disclosed her next role. Juneja had led category marketing for Maggi Noodles since March 2024. She joined Nestlé in September 2020 as Marketing Manager for Maggi Flavor World and Digital Head for Maggi, working on products including spices, coconut milk and stock cubes. Before Nestlé, she held brand and category roles at GSK Consumer Healthcare India, working across the Horlicks portfolio. Earlier, she worked on ITC’s Sunfeast business. Shilpa Jain steps down as Nykaa’s AVP, Consumer & Market Insights Shilpa Jain has stepped down as Associate Vice-President, Consumer & Market Insights, at Nykaa after five years. Her next role has not been disclosed. Jain joined Nykaa in 2021. Her work there focused on consumer research, market insights and changes in consumer behaviour. Before Nykaa, she spent nearly two years at Google as a Consumer & Marketing Specialist. She previously worked at Coca-Cola and Kantar in consumer research and market insights. Inspira Global appoints Neha Phale as Group Head, Marketing Communications Neha Phale Inspira Global has appointed Neha Phale as Group Head, Marketing Communications. She will oversee corporate and internal communications, brand messaging and stakeholder engagement across the group. Her remit covers Inspira Global’s businesses, including Inspira Realty, Lenexis FoodWorks, Inspira EXIM and SEVA Home. She will work with their leadership teams on communications across the group. Phale has more than 20 years of experience. Before joining Inspira Global, she held senior communications roles at VVF India and Huhtamaki, and earlier worked at Welspun India, Huntsman International and Dow Chemicals. Ashish Nagpal joins International Tractors as Head of Marketing, International Business Ashish Nagpal has joined International Tractors (ITL) as Head of Marketing, International Business, after 12 years at Bajaj Auto. He announced the move on LinkedIn. Nagpal will oversee international marketing for ITL, which sells tractors under the Sonalika and Solis brands. At Bajaj Auto, he was most recently General Manager and Category Marketing Head for its commercial vehicle portfolio. He also handled marketing across Latin American markets during his time at Bajaj Auto. Earlier, Nagpal worked at Hindustan Coca-Cola Beverages, Wrigley and Eveready Industries. Nucleus Software appoints Sudhanshu Tripathi as Chief Marketing Officer Sudhanshu Tripathi Nucleus Software has appointed Sudhanshu Tripathi as Chief Marketing Officer. Tripathi will oversee global marketing, including brand positioning, demand generation, analyst engagement and partner programmes. Nucleus Software provides lending and transaction banking platforms to banks and financial institutions. He joins from Quick Heal Technologies, where he was Chief Marketing Officer and Head of ESG. He previously held roles at Sterlite Power, Cyient, FINO PayTech and Tata Consultancy Services. Trehan IRIS appoints Prasad Rane as Chief Business & Marketing Officer Prasad Rane Trehan IRIS has appointed Prasad Rane as Chief Business & Marketing Officer. He will oversee commercial strategy, sales, marketing and customer experience. Rane joins from DailyObjects, where he was Chief Growth Officer and worked on retail expansion and new business channels. Earlier, he held roles at ICS Group, including Chief Marketing Officer at PPZ and CEO of SPACES. His experience spans real estate, retail and consumer businesses. Shaisang Maniar joins WPP Media as Associate Vice President, Media Solutions Shaisang Maniar has joined WPP Media as Associate Vice President, Media Solutions. He announced the appointment on LinkedIn. Maniar was previously Qube Cinema’s Region Head, Sales for Gujarat, where he oversaw advertising revenue and market expansion. Before that, he spent more than five years at Mirchi in Ahmedabad, rising from Senior Account Manager to Group Manager. He has also worked at SOI Live Marketing & Events and infoAnalytica Consulting. Kanika Bains joins Publicis Groupe as VP and Head of People & Culture for MSL India Kanika Bains has joined MSL India as Vice-President and Head of People & Culture. She announced the appointment on LinkedIn. Bains previously spent more than four years at Edelman as Vice-President of Talent Acquisition, overseeing hiring in India and selected roles across Singapore, Australia, Hong Kong and Malaysia. Earlier, she led talent acquisition at Reliance Brands and held recruitment roles at Paytm for more than a decade. MSL is Publicis Groupe’s public relations and integrated communications network. Parul Budhiraja joins Ogilvy as Executive Vice President Parul Budhiraja has joined Ogilvy as Executive Vice President, she announced on LinkedIn. Details of her responsibilities have not been disclosed. Before joining Ogilvy, Budhiraja worked as an independent marketing consultant from April 2024 to September 2026. She was also Principal Strategist at Branduits during that period. Earlier, she spent nearly three years at Cheil India, where she served as General Manager, and more than five years at Contract India, where she rose to Vice President. Dentsu appoints Vidhu Ravinath and Archisman Sarangi to lead Performance Studio (L) Vidhu Ravinath and Archisman Sarangi (R) Dentsu India has appointed Vidhu Ravinath and Archisman Sarangi as Vice President and Business Head of its newly launched Dentsu Performance Studio. The Bengaluru-based unit combines creative development, production, performance media and measurement. Ravinath and Sarangi will oversee its operations and use campaign data to inform subsequent creative work. Dentsu said the studio operates from a 3,000 sq ft facility and aims to produce more than 1,000 assets a month. Abhishek Shetty joins Grab as Regional Director & Head of Product Marketing Abhishek Shetty Abhishek Shetty has joined Grab as Regional Director and Head of Product Marketing, he announced on LinkedIn. He will be based in Singapore, with a remit across the company’s Southeast Asian markets. His role covers product marketing for Grab’s mobility, delivery, financial services and commerce businesses, including product positioning and plans to bring products to market. Shetty was previously Marketing Head for Swiggy Instamart and private brands. He has also held marketing roles at SonyLIV and Celio India. InsuranceDekho elevates Alisha K to AVP, Brand and Marketing InsuranceDekho has elevated Alisha K to Associate Vice-President, Brand and Marketing. She announced the move on LinkedIn. At InsuranceDekho, she worked on the "Khul Kar Khelo" campaign featuring Sourav Ganguly, who became the company’s brand ambassador in July 2026. She was also involved in the InsuranceDekho Cup in Sri Lanka. Before joining InsuranceDekho, Alisha worked on marketing and product launches at INDmoney. Her earlier roles included marketing communications at Home Credit India and content and brand partnerships at Leverage Edu. Disha Sanghvi joins Sarvam to lead brand and communications Disha Sanghvi Disha Sanghvi has joined AI company Sarvam to lead brand and communications, she announced on LinkedIn. Sanghvi was previously General Manager and Head of Marketing Communication and PR at fintech company ZET. Her work there covered brand marketing, public relations, content and product messaging. She has also held content, communications and brand roles at PhonePe, Onsurity, Digit Insurance and Exide Life Insurance. Earlier in her career, she reported on personal finance for Mint. DailyObjects appoints Zeenah Vilcassim as Global Chief Marketing Officer Zeenah Vilcassim DailyObjects has appointed Zeenah Vilcassim as Global Chief Marketing Officer. She will lead its brand and marketing strategy as the company seeks to expand beyond India. Vilcassim joins after leading marketing for Nothing in India. Before that, she was CEO of Zomato Live, the business now known as District by Zomato. She has more than 17 years of experience across consumer marketing, brand strategy and business development in India and international markets. Earlier in her career, Vilcassim was Chief Marketing Officer at Bacardi India, overseeing marketing across its portfolio. She also served as Bacardi’s Global Brand Director for Whiskies, working on strategy across international markets. Logitech appoints Vikrant Malik as Marketing Head Logitech has appointed Vikrant Malik as Marketing Head. Malik announced the move on LinkedIn and said he would work on category development and the company’s product portfolio in India. He joins from Haleon, where he was Expert Marketing Lead for the India Subcontinent from July 2022 to August 2026. Before that, he spent more than four years at GSK Consumer Healthcare India in marketing roles spanning oral health, respiratory health, pain relief and supplements. At GSK Consumer Healthcare, Malik also managed marketing for Sensodyne. Earlier in his career, he co-founded Neighbee, a platform for citizen volunteer groups, and worked at PK Online Ventures. Carat appoints Sarah Stringer as Global Chief Strategy and Innovation Officer Sarah Stringer (L) and Bram Meuleman (R) Carat has appointed Sarah Stringer as Global Chief Strategy and Innovation Officer and promoted Bram Meuleman to Global Chief Planning and Intelligence Officer. Stringer was previously Global Chief of Innovation at dentsu Media and has held leadership roles at Carat in the US and Australia. Meuleman was Carat’s Global Head of Strategy and earlier worked at dentsu X. The two will work with Carat Global Brand President Chrissie Hanson on strategy, planning and innovation, the agency said. Himanshu Shekhar takes charge of VEGA’s digital and D2C business VEGA has appointed Himanshu Shekhar as Head of Digital, D2C and Growth. Shekhar joins from Livguard, where he was Head of Digital Marketing. His work there covered online sales, customer relationship management, marketplaces and media investment. He previously served as Digital Marketing Lead at Usha International and Business Performance Manager at Publicis Media. Earlier, he held digital marketing roles at Google. BEI Confluence elevates Abhishek Gupta to Managing Director BEI Confluence appointed Abhishek Gupta as Managing Director, effective August 2026. He will lead the agency’s operations and report to its Board. Founder Tapas Gupta stepped down as Managing Director after 27 years in the role. He will remain Chairman and continue to mentor the agency. Abhishek Gupta has more than 20 years of experience in brand strategy, digital marketing and business leadership, including earlier roles at Havas, Publicis Worldwide and Ogilvy. At BEI Confluence, his responsibilities include talent development, client partnerships and business growth.

title: NCW Chief Vijaya Rahatkar interacts with working women in Gwalior
excerpt: Gwalior, Sep 26 (IANS) National Commission for Women Chairperson Vijaya Rahatkar on Saturday began a four-day visit to Madhya Pradesh from Gwalior where she interacted with working women and discussed issues related to empowerment. In a message on X, Rahatkar shared details of her schedule and said, “Starting today, I am beginning a four-day tour of Madhya Pradesh. During this journey, I will have the opportunity to participate in many programs being organised in Gwalior and Shivpuri districts.” “By travelling to every corner of the country to infuse new energy into the campaign for women's empowerment, by meeting women at the grassroots level and engaging in conversations with them, and by closely understanding their hopes and experiences —this is my small effort,” she said on X. Her engagements in Gwalior over two days include a visit to Central Jail, Lakshmibai National Institute of Physical Education and Shri Pitambara Peeth near Datia Railway Station. Meetings with local representatives and interaction with Maharashtra Samaj in Jayendraganj, Shinde Ki Chhawani were also scheduled. On the third day of her visit to Shivpuri, Rahatkar is scheduled to undertake a “Mahila Jansunvai”; lead consultations on state specific women related issues, visit a Sakhi One Stop Centre and chair a review meeting with senior district administrative and police officials at the collectorate meeting hall. On the final day of her state visit, the NCW Chairperson will be back in Gwalior to hold a “Mahila Jansunvai”, interact with district administrative and police officials and take part in “Yadhodha AI” and “She Serves” programmes involving the youth at LNIPE and a private university. Earlier, Rahatkar visited Hussainiwala Border in Punjab’s Ferozepur. In a message on X, she said, “My visit to Hussainiwala Border, Ferozepur (Punjab) was not just a trip for me, but an unforgettable experience of pride and gratitude toward the nation.” “When I reached the Hussainiwala border and saw that the border of another country was just a few steps away, a deep feeling stirred in my heart—that our citizens are so secure because our border guardians are protecting the country with such vigilance and dedication,” she said. After a visit to the National Martyrs Memorial, she wrote, “The visit to the National Martyrs Memorial at Hussainiwala was an extremely emotional experience for me. On this sacred land, the echoes of the sacrifice of martyrs Bhagat Singh, Rajguru, and Sukhdev can still be felt today.” “Seeing their letters and documents preserved in the museum deeply touched my heart. In these letters, the indomitable courage of those three young revolutionaries and their resolve to dedicate their lives to the nation are evident. The youth of today should draw inspiration from this selfless patriotism and play their role in building the country,” she said. “Visiting the samadhi of Martyr Bhagat Singh's mother, Vidyavati Ji, was a particularly poignant moment for me. For a mother, losing her child is the greatest sorrow, and perhaps the greatest pride could be that her son devoted his life to the nation. Expressing that maternal pain and maternal pride in words is difficult,” said Rahatkar. --IANS rch/uk
